identity.title: How to train your microbe: editing environmental bacteria.

content.abstract: Genome editing is an essential tool in microbiology, enabling researchers to assess gene function, link genotype to phenotype, and design microbes with specific features. Most tools have been developed in model bacteria, and adapting them to environmental species remains time- and resource-intensive. This review provides a framework for engineering environmental bacteria, including assessment of genetic tractability, considerations for overcoming challenges in recalcitrant systems, and an overview of techniques with guidance on tool selection. We discuss the emerging field of microbiome editing, where genome modifications can be delivered to bacteria within complex microbial communities and hosts, opening new possibilities for mechanistic studies across diverse environments. These advances promise to shift functional microbiology from reductionist, isolate-based approaches toward contextually informed, mechanistic investigations.
